newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila police, military mend fences on drugs issue.
newsitem.headline: Manila police, military mend fences on drugs issue.

text.p: Philippine police and military officials who were squabbling among themselves over who should lead the anti-drugs campaign agreed on Monday to set aside their differences.

A government statement said Defense Secretary Renato de Villa who heads the military and Local Government Secretary Roberto Barbers who heads the police had agreed to let the Department of Justice lead the government's fight against illegal drugs.
The two departments had traded accusations last week after a businessman in military custody named 15 police officers as being part of a drug syndicate.
The statement angered the police department which said military officials may have planted it to damage their reputation.

"Utmost effort shall be exerted by all concerned to avoid any misunderstanding, irritants or conflict among operating units. Accordingly, any unresolved issue shall be immediately elevated to higher authority," a memorandum signed by the secretaries said.
President Fidel Ramos told the two warring agencies to stop the squabbling.

"It is part of your sacred duty to stand fast and overcome these challenges regardless of the brickbats, and the flak and the shelling and the demolition now being carried out against all of you," Ramos told military and police officers.
"It is not, I'm sure, in our national interrest to allow the constant heckling and unfair criticism and unjustified destruction of the reputation of both institutions," Ramos added.
